label: Frequency and predictive role of intestinal parasitic infections with irritable bowel syndrome in Egyptian patients: a case-control study.
summary: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction with multifactorial pathophysiology, including post-infectious mechanisms. In endemic regions, intestinal parasitic infections remain highly frequent and may contribute to persistent gastrointestinal symptoms; however, their role in IBS is often under-recognized and insufficiently studied.
